section-85-1.FOR: any Special Health Authority, National Health Service trust or NHS foundation trust or a local authority in England in the exercise of education functions (“the accommodating authority”)
section-85-1.TO: notify the appropriate officer of the responsible authority
section-85-1.WHERE: a child is provided with accommodation in England by the accommodating authority — (a) for a consecutive period of at least three months; or (b) with the intention, on the part of that authority, of accommodating him for such a period

section-85-2.TO: notify the appropriate officer of the responsible authority when they cease to accommodate a child
section-85-2.WHERE: subsection (1) applies with respect to the child

section-85-4.TO: — (a) take such steps as are reasonably practicable to enable them to determine whether the child’s welfare is adequately safeguarded and promoted while he is accommodated by the accommodating authority; and (b) consider the extent to which (if at all) they should exercise any of their functions under this Act with respect to the child
section-85-4.WHERE: the appropriate officer of the local authority has been notified under this section, or under section 120 of the Social Services and Well-being (Wales) Act 2014 (assessment of children accommodated by health authorities and education authorities)

section-86-1.FOR: the person carrying on the establishment in question
section-86-1.TO: notify the appropriate officer of the local authority within whose area the establishment is carried on
section-86-1.WHERE: a child is provided with accommodation in England in any care home or independent hospital — (a) for a consecutive period of at least three months; or (b) with the intention, on the part of the person taking the decision to accommodate him, of accommodating him for such period

section-86-2.FOR: the person carrying on the establishment
section-86-2.TO: notify the appropriate officer of that authority when he ceases to accommodate a child in the establishment
section-86-2.WHERE: subsection (1) applies with respect to the child

section-86-3.TO: — (a) take such steps as are reasonably practicable to enable them to determine whether the child’s welfare is adequately safeguarded and promoted while he is accommodated in the establishment in question; and (b) consider the extent to which (if at all) they should exercise any of their functions under this Act with respect to the child
section-86-3.WHERE: the appropriate officer of the local authority has been notified under this section

section-86-4.FOR: the person carrying on any care home or independent hospital
section-86-4.TO: fail, without reasonable excuse, to comply with this section

section-86-5.FOR: a person authorised by a local authority in England
section-86-5.TO: enter any care home or independent hospital within the authority’s area
section-86-5.FOR_2: the purpose of establishing whether the requirements of this section have been complied with

section-86-6.TO: intentionally obstruct another in the exercise of the power of entry

section-86-7.FOR: Any person exercising the power of entry
section-86-7.TO: produce some duly authenticated document showing his authority to do so

section-86A-2.TO: make arrangements for the child to be visited by a representative of the authority (“a representative”)

section-86A-3.TO: provide advice and assistance to the local authority on the performance of their duties under section 85(4) or, as the case may be, 86(3)

section-86A-4.TO: make provision about— (a) the frequency of visits under visiting arrangements; (b) circumstances in which visiting arrangements must require a child to be visited; and (c) additional functions of a representative

section-86A-5.TO: be made by the Secretary of State

section-86A-6.TO: satisfy themselves that the person chosen has the necessary skills and experience to perform the functions of a representative

section-87-1.TO: safeguard and promote any child’s welfare
section-87-1.WHERE: a school or college provides accommodation for the child

section-87-3.TO: take such steps as are reasonably practicable to enable any school or college to determine whether a child’s welfare is adequately safeguarded and promoted while accommodation for the child is provided by the school or college
section-87-3.WHERE: accommodation is provided for the child by them

section-87-3A.TO: direct the Chief Inspector for England to take the steps referred to in subsection (3)
section-87-3A.WHERE: accommodation is provided for a child by a school or college in England
section-87-3A.AT: any time (including a time when the duty under subsection (3) is suspended by virtue of section 87A)

section-87-3B.TO: take the steps referred to in subsection (3)
section-87-3B.WHERE: accommodation is provided for a child by a school or college in Wales
section-87-3B.AT: any time when the duty under subsection (3) is suspended by virtue of section 87A

section-87-4.TO: — (a) in the case of a school other than an independent school, an alternative provision Academy that is not an independent school or a special school, notify the local authority for the area in which the school is situated; (b) in the case of a special school which is maintained by a local authority, notify that authority; (c) in any other case, notify the Secretary of State
section-87-4.WHERE: he is of the opinion that there has been a failure to comply with subsection (1) in relation to a child provided with accommodation by a school or college in England

section-87-4A.TO: — (a) in the case of a school other than an independent school or a special school, notify the local authority for the area in which the school is situated; (b) in the case of a special school which is maintained by a local authority, notify that authority
section-87-4A.WHERE: they are of the opinion that there has been a failure to comply with subsection (1) in relation to a child provided with accommodation by a school or college in Wales

section-87-5.FOR: a person authorised by the appropriate authority
section-87-5.TO: enter premises which are, or are to be, premises of the school or college.
section-87-5.FOR_2: the purpose of enabling that authority to discharge any of its functions under this section
section-87-5.WHERE: accommodation is, or is to be, provided for a child by any school or college

section-87-6.FOR: Any person exercising the power conferred by subsection (5)
section-87-6.TO: carry out such inspection of premises, children and records as is prescribed by regulations made by the Secretary of State for the purposes of this section

section-87-7.TO: produce some duly authenticated document showing his authority to do so

section-87-8.FOR: Any person authorised by the regulations to inspect records
section-87-8.TO: be entitled to have access to, and inspect and check the operation of, any computer and any associated apparatus or material which is or has been in use in connection with the records in question

section-87-8.FOR: Any person authorised by the regulations to inspect records
section-87-8.TO: require— (i) the person by whom or on whose behalf the computer is or has been so used; or (ii) any person having charge of, or otherwise concerned with the operation of, the computer, apparatus or material, to afford him such assistance as he may reasonably require

section-87-9.TO: intentionally obstruct another in the exercise of any power conferred by this section or the regulations

section-87-9A.FOR: the Chief Inspector for England or the National Assembly for Wales
section-87-9A.TO: publish a report on whether the child’s welfare is adequately safeguarded and promoted while accommodation for the child is provided by the school or college
section-87-9A.WHERE: that authority exercises the power conferred by subsection (5) in relation to a child

section-87-9B.FOR: the Chief Inspector for England or the National Assembly for Wales
section-87-9B.TO: — (a) send a copy of the report to the school or college concerned; and (b) make copies of the report available for inspection at its offices by any person at any reasonable time
section-87-9B.WHERE: it publishes a report under this section

section-87A-1.TO: appoint a person to be an inspector
section-87A-1.IF: — (a) that person already acts as an inspector for other purposes in relation to schools or colleges to which section 87(1) applies, and (b) the Secretary of State is satisfied that the person is an appropriate person to determine whether the welfare of children provided with accommodation by such schools or colleges is adequately safeguarded and promoted while accommodation for the children is provided by them

section-87A-4.TO: terminate a person’s appointment under subsection (1)
section-87A-4.IF: — (a) that person so requests, or (b) the Secretary of State ceases, in relation to that person, to be satisfied that he is such a person as is mentioned in paragraph (b) of that subsection

section-87A-4.TO: give notice of the termination of that person’s appointment to the appropriate authority

section-87A-4A.TO: by regulations specify matters that must be taken into account in deciding whether to appoint a person to be an inspector for the purposes of this section in relation to schools or colleges in England, or to terminate the appointment of such a person under subsection (4)(b)

section-87A-5.TO: give to the appropriate authority notice in writing of the fact that it has ceased to have effect
section-87A-5.WHERE: — (a) the appropriate authority’s duty under section 87(3) in relation to any school or college is suspended under this section, and (b) the relevant agreement ceases to have effect

section-87B-1.TO: impose on a person appointed under section 87A(1) (“an authorised inspector”) such requirements relating to, or in connection with, the carrying out under substitution agreements of the function mentioned in section 87A(2)(b) as the Secretary of State thinks fit

section-87B-2.TO: give notice of that fact (a) in the case of a school other than an independent school, an alternative provision Academy that is not an independent school or a special school, to the local authority for the area in which the school is situated; (b) in the case of a special school which is maintained by a local authority, to that authority; (c) in any other case, to the Secretary of State
section-87B-2.WHERE: it appears to the inspector that there has been a failure to comply with section 87(1) in the case of a child provided with accommodation by the school or college to which the agreement relates
section-87B-2.IN THE COURSE OF: carrying out under a substitution agreement the function mentioned in section 87A(2)(b)

section-87B-3.TO: — (a) give notice of that fact to the local authority in whose area the school or college is situated, and (b) where the inspector is required to make inspection reports to the Secretary of State, supply that local authority with a copy of the latest inspection report to have been made by the inspector to the Secretary of State in relation to the school or college
section-87B-3.WHERE: it appears to the inspector that a child provided with accommodation by the school or college to which the agreement relates is suffering, or is likely to suffer, significant harm
section-87B-3.IN THE COURSE OF: carrying out under a substitution agreement the function mentioned in section 87A(2)(b)

section-87BA-1.TO: prepare and send to the Secretary of State a report about inspectors who are appointed under section 87A in relation to schools or colleges in England
section-87BA-1.AT: intervals of no more than a year

section-87BA-2.TO: have regard to such matters as the Secretary of State may direct
section-87BA-2.IN: preparing a report under this section

section-87BA-3.TO: give directions about— (a) matters to be taken into account in preparing a report, and (b) the form and contents of a report

section-87C-1.TO: prepare and publish statements of national minimum standards for safeguarding and promoting the welfare of children for whom accommodation is provided by a school or college

section-87C-2.TO: keep the standards set out in the statements under review
publish amended statements whenever he considers it appropriate to do so

section-87C-3.TO: consult any persons he considers appropriate
section-87C-3.BEFORE: issuing a statement, or an amended statement which in the opinion of the Secretary of State effects a substantial change in the standards

section-87C-4.TO: be taken into account— (a) in the making by the appropriate authority of any determination under section 87(4) or (4A); (b) in the making by a person appointed under section 87A(1) of any determination under section 87B(2); and (c) in any proceedings under any other enactment in which it is alleged that the person has failed to comply with section 87(1)

section-87D-1.TO: be made in relation to any school or college in respect of which the appropriate authority is required to take steps under section 87(3)

section-87D-2.TO: by regulations require the relevant person to pay the appropriate authority an annual fee of such amount, and within such time, as the regulations may specify

section-87D-3.FOR: a fee payable by virtue of this section
section-87D-3.TO: without prejudice to any other method of recovery, be recovered summarily as a civil debt

section-91-14.TO: (whether or not it makes any other order in response to the application) order that no application for an order under this Act of any specified kind may be made with respect to the child concerned by any person named in the order without leave of the court
section-91-14.ON: disposing of any application for an order under this Act

section-91-15.FOR: a further application of a kind mentioned in paragraphs (a) to (e)

section-91-17.TO: make a further application for an order under section 34 with respect to the same child
section-91-17.WHERE: — (a) the person has made an application for such an order; (b) the application has been refused; and (c) a period of less than six months has elapsed since the refusal

section-91A-4.TO: consider whether there has been a material change of circumstances since the order was made
section-91A-4.WHERE: a person who is named in a section 91(14) order applies for leave to make an application of a specified kind

section-91A-5.TO: make a section 91(14) order— (a) on an application made— (i) by the relevant individual; (ii) by or on behalf of the child concerned; (iii) by any other person who is a party to the application being disposed of by the court; (b) of its own motion

section-93-1.FOR: An authority having power to make rules of court
section-93-1.TO: make such provision for giving effect to— (a) this Act; (b) the provisions of any statutory instrument made under this Act; or (c) any amendment made by this Act in any other enactment, as appears to that authority to be necessary or expedient

section-93-2.TO: make provision— (a) with respect to the procedure to be followed in any relevant proceedings (including the manner in which any application is to be made or other proceedings commenced); (b) as to the persons entitled to participate in any relevant proceedings, whether as parties to the proceedings or by being given the opportunity to make representations to the court; (bb) for children to be separately represented in relevant proceedings, (c) with respect to the documents and information to be furnished, and notices to be given, in connection with any relevant proceedings; (e) with respect to preliminary hearings; (h) enabling the court, in such circumstances as may be prescribed, to proceed on any application even though the respondent has not been given notice of the proceedings

section-95-1.TO: order the child concerned to attend such stage or stages of the proceedings as may be specified in the order
section-95-1.IN: any proceedings in which the court is hearing an application for an order under Part IV or V, or is considering whether to make any such order

section-95-2.TO: be exercised in accordance with rules of court

section-95-4.TO: make an order authorising a constable, or such person as may be specified in the order— (a) to take charge of the child and to bring him to the court; and (b) to enter and search any premises specified in the order if he has reasonable cause to believe that the child may be found on the premises

section-95-5.TO: order any person who is in a position to do so to bring the child to the court

section-95-6.TO: order a person to disclose information about the whereabouts of the child to the court
section-95-6.WHERE: the court has reason to believe that the person has information about it

section-96-2.IF: in its opinion— (a) he understands that it is his duty to speak the truth; and (b) he has sufficient understanding to justify his evidence being heard

section-96-3.TO: with the concurrence of the Lord Chief Justice, by order make provision for the admissibility of evidence which would otherwise be inadmissible under any rule of law relating to hearsay

section-96-4.TO: only be made with respect to— (a) civil proceedings in general or such civil proceedings, or class of civil proceedings, as may be prescribed; and (b) evidence in connection with the upbringing, maintenance or welfare of a child

section-96-5.TO: provide for the admissibility of statements which are made orally or in a prescribed form or which are recorded by any prescribed method of recording
make different provision for different purposes and in relation to different descriptions of court

make such amendments and repeals in any enactment relating to evidence (other than in this Act) as the Lord Chancellor considers necessary or expedient in consequence of the provision made by the order

section-97-2.TO: publish to the public at large or any section of the public any material which is intended, or likely, to identify— (a) any child as being involved in any proceedings before the High Court or the family court in which any power under this Act or the Adoption and Children Act 2002 may be exercised by the court with respect to that or any other child; or (b) an address or school as being that of a child involved in any such proceedings

section-97-3.TO: prove that he did not know, and had no reason to suspect, that the published material was intended, or likely, to identify the child
section-97-3.IN: any proceedings for an offence under this section

section-97-4.FOR: The court or the Lord Chancellor
section-97-4.TO: by order dispense with the requirements of subsection (2) to such extent as may be specified in the order
section-97-4.IF: satisfied that the welfare of the child requires it and, in the case of the Lord Chancellor, if the Lord Chief Justice agrees

section-97-6A.TO: — (a) enter material in the Adoption and Children Act Register (established under section 125 of the Adoption and Children Act 2002), or (b) permit persons to search and inspect that register pursuant to regulations made under section 128A of that Act

section-97-9.TO: nominate a judicial office holder (as defined in section 109(4) of the Constitutional Reform Act 2005) to exercise his functions under subsection (4)

section-98-1.TO: be excused from— (a) giving evidence on any matter; or (b) answering any question put to him in the course of his giving evidence, on the ground that doing so might incriminate him or his spouse or civil partner of an offence
section-98-1.IN: any proceedings in which a court is hearing an application for an order under Part IV or V

section-98-2.FOR: A statement or admission made in such proceedings

section-100-2.TO: exercise the High Court’s inherent jurisdiction with respect to children

section-100-2.TO: exercise the High Court’s inherent jurisdiction with respect to children
section-100-2.SO AS TO: require a child to be accommodated by or on behalf of a local authority

section-100-2.TO: exercise the High Court’s inherent jurisdiction with respect to children— (a) so as to require a child to be placed in the care, or put under the supervision, of a local authority
section-100-2.SO AS TO: make a child who is the subject of a care order a ward of court

section-100-2.TO: exercise the High Court’s inherent jurisdiction with respect to children
section-100-2.FOR_2: the purpose of conferring on any local authority power to determine any question which has arisen, or which may arise, in connection with any aspect of parental responsibility for a child

section-100-3.TO: make an application for any exercise of the court’s inherent jurisdiction with respect to children
section-100-3.UNLESS: the authority have obtained the leave of the court

section-101-1.TO: make regulations providing— (a) for prescribed orders which— (i) are made by a court in Northern Ireland; and (ii) appear to the Secretary of State to correspond in their effect to orders which may be made under any provision of this Act, to have effect in prescribed circumstances, for prescribed purposes of this Act, as if they were orders of a prescribed kind made under this Act; (b) for prescribed orders which— (i) are made by a court in England and Wales; and (ii) appear to the Secretary of State to correspond in their effect to orders which may be made under any provision in force in Northern Ireland, to have effect in prescribed circumstances, for prescribed purposes of the law of Northern Ireland, as if they were orders of a prescribed kind made in Northern Ireland

section-101-2.TO: provide for the order concerned to cease to have effect
section-101-2.FOR_2: the purposes of the law of Northern Ireland, or (as the case may be) the law of England and Wales

section-101-3.TO: make regulations providing for prescribed orders which— (a) are made by a court in the Isle of Man or in any of the Channel Islands; and (b) appear to the Secretary of State to correspond in their effect to orders which may be made under this Act, to have effect in prescribed circumstances for prescribed purposes of this Act, as if they were orders of a prescribed kind made under this Act

section-101-5.FOR: Any regulations made under this section
section-101-5.TO: — (a) make such consequential amendments (including repeals) in— (i) section 25 of the Children and Young Persons Act 1969 (transfers between England and Wales and Northern Ireland); or (ii) section 26 (transfers between England and Wales and Channel Islands or Isle of Man) of that Act, as the Secretary of State considers necessary or expedient; and — (b) modify any provision of this Act, in its application (by virtue of the regulations) in relation to an order made otherwise than in England and Wales

section-102-1.TO: issue a warrant authorising any constable to assist that person in the exercise of those powers, using reasonable force if necessary

section-102-1.ON: an application made by any person for a warrant under this section

section-102-2.FOR: Every warrant issued under this section

section-102-2.IF: — (a) that person so desires; and (b) the court by whom the warrant is issued does not direct otherwise

section-102-3.FOR: A court granting an application for a warrant under this section

section-102-4.FOR: An application for a warrant under this section

section-102-5.FOR: an application for a warrant under this section and any warrant granted on the application

section-102-5.FOR: an application for a warrant under this section and any warrant granted on the application
section-102-5.TO: describe him as clearly as possible
